# Whether a point is a member of a ball, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_contains_point_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The three-valued answer to whether the point $t = t_0 + t_1$ is a finite number and a member of $X$, $X$ the ball of center $c = c_0 + c_1$ and radius $r$: *yes* only if it holds, *no* only if it fails, otherwise *unknown*, both masks false:

$$\mathit{yes} \implies t = t_0 + t_1 \in X, \qquad \mathit{no} \implies t = t_0 + t_1 \notin X.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $t = t_0 + t_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `member(t, X)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Trit` | yes, no or unknown; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `member(t, X)` | `T`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Trit` | yes, no or unknown; the point made a number of two limbs by `make_2` first, exactly: a composition of two proved kernels, not machine-checked as one statement; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.contains(t)` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` | $\mathit{yes}$; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.contains(t)` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `T` | `bool` | $\mathit{yes}$; the point made a number of two limbs by `make_2` first, exactly: a composition of two proved kernels, not machine-checked as one statement; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c$ and radius $r$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $t$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{yes}$ is true only if $t = t_0 + t_1 \in X$; $\mathit{no}$ only if $t = t_0 + t_1 \notin X$; never both. Both false is the answer *unknown*.
- When an operand is the empty set or the whole line, or the point is not a finite number, the answer is exact: each mask is true exactly when its relation holds.
- For finite operands the answer may be *unknown* although one of the relations holds, close to where it stops holding: certain, not exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_contains_point_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallContains2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallContains2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_contains_point_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_contains_point_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds of the distance by add_ball_2_2 compared with the radius (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_contains_point_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_contains_point_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`abs_upper_2`](abs_upper_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md), [`abs_2`](abs_2.md), [`to_down_2`](to_down_2.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

```
# Whether a 2-limb value t is a member of a ball with a 2-limb center, three-valued (milestone2.md,
# "One enclosure interface", "Certain", the listing ball_contains_point_2): with (z, e) =
# add_ball_2_2(t, -c), |(t - c) - z| <= e, so hi = radd(abs_upper_2(z), e) is at least |t - c| and
# lo = sub_down_1(to_down_2(abs_2(z)), e) at most it; yes = hi <= r, no = r < lo, never both. The
# page's listing, with lo written as minus the rounding up of e - to_down_2(abs_2(z)), the same
# value, so that the radius e, a fused result, is not negated (a rule of the generator); and two
# masks more for the operands that are not finite: no is true for the empty set and for a point that
# is not a finite number, of which no ball has a member (the whole line contains every finite point,
# which yes says). Certain, not exact: undecided within about 2e of the boundary (e: a few
# u^2 |t - c| and twice the smallest normal number) plus three gaps of T at the radius or at the
# distance, whichever is larger (the bounds hi and lo are numbers of T; architecture.md, "Claims of
# the enclosure interface: predicates and comparisons", gives the band as measured). The band is not
# claimed.

nc0         = neg(c0)
nc1         = neg(c1)
(z0, z1, e) = add_ball_2_2(t0, t1, nc0, nc1)
au          = abs_upper_2(z0, z1)
hi          = radd(au, e)
(w0, w1)    = abs_2(z0, z1)
wd          = to_down_2(w0, w1)
nw          = neg(wd)
tl          = add_up_1(e, nw)
lo          = neg(tl)
yes         = le(hi, r)
na          = lt(r, lo)
ta          = abs(t0)
ft          = lt(ta, const inf)
ne          = eq(r, r)
ok          = and(ft, ne)
nk          = not(ok)
no          = or(na, nk)
```
